title: When the Colony Breaks
premise: Casper Crane, the last navigator aboard the derelict survey ship Vesperine, has spent eleven years maintaining a beacon whose original commissioning records were scrubbed from every database. When the entire system's gravity stutters for nine seconds, Casper discovers the beacon was never a lighthouse at all—it was a lock, and the backups sleeping in the hold are the keys. Pursued by a salvage syndicate that wants the ship's cargo of stored minds, and accompanied by Ila, an archivist who fell in love with a version of Casper she can no longer be sure is the original, Casper must pilot the dying Vesperine to a relay at the edge of dead space. There, Casper learns they are themselves a backup—the fourth—and must choose between restoring the original's memory (and losing Ila) or remaining the person they have become. In the end, Casper breaks the lock, frees the sleeping minds, and lets the beacon go dark, choosing an unrecorded life with Ila over the duty of being anyone's original.
about_author: Ansel Whitlock is a former maritime cartographer who turned to science fiction after a decade charting coastlines that kept disappearing from the maps. He writes quiet, aching stories about people who maintain things nobody remembers building.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Hours
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishes the Vesperine's decayed routines, the humming hold full of backup pods, and the beacon Casper winds like a clock nobody wound before. Emotional beat: lonely devotion disguised as habit.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Gravity across the system flickers for exactly nine seconds; the beacon's frequency shifts in response, and Casper realizes it answered something. Emotional beat: dread blooming under wonder.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. A salvage skiff docks uninvited; Ila Voss arrives claiming to be researching decommissioned beacons, and freezes when she sees Casper's face. Emotional beat: recognition she can't explain.

chapters.title: Records That Erase Themselves
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Ila reveals the beacon's commissioning file self-deleted across every archive the moment she queried it. Casper denies knowing anything. Emotional beat: the first crack in Casper's careful ignorance.

chapters.title: What Sleeps in the Hold
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper finally descends to the backup bay: forty pods, forty faces, and one that is unmistakably Casper's own. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-estrangement.

chapters.title: Ila's Version of Me
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Pressured by Casper, Ila admits she knew a Casper Crane years ago on Meridian Station—and loved him. Emotional beat: grief for a person who may be standing in front of her.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Wake
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A syndicate cruiser, the Halcyon Ledger, enters the system broadcasting a salvage claim on the Vesperine. Emotional beat: the invisible life ending on a schedule.

chapters.title: Cargo of Minds
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Ila deciphers partial manifests: the backups aren't copies of crew—they're a colony's stored minds, smuggled out of a war no one names anymore. Emotional beat: moral weight settling on both of them.

chapters.title: Wind the Beacon
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The beacon begins failing; Casper's maintenance rituals are revealed as something deeper—muscle memory from a life Casper doesn't remember living. Emotional beat: the body remembering what the mind was denied.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. The Ledger's captain, Ondine Marsh, offers Ila passage out if she delivers the ship. Ila stalls. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The beacon's final transmission decodes to coordinates: a relay in dead space that can wake the backups—or erase them. Emotional beat: purpose arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Burn Calculation
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper plots a course through a debris shoal; the Vesperine is too slow unless they strip the hold, and stripping it might kill the sleepers. Emotional beat: arithmetic versus conscience.

chapters.title: Ila Decides to Stay
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Ila burns her own extraction window and stays aboard, telling herself it's for the archive. Emotional beat: love admitting itself sideways.

chapters.title: First Contact, Second Hand
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A backup pod briefly wakes—a woman named Sef who recognizes Casper and calls them 'Four.' Emotional beat: the word Four landing like a verdict.

chapters.title: The Ledger Closes In
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Marsh's boarding party latches to the hull during the debris transit. Emotional beat: hunted intimacy, hands held in the dark.

chapters.title: EVA in the Shoal
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper spacewalks to cut the boarding tethers and nearly drifts into the shoal; Ila talks them home by radio. Emotional beat: trust forged at the end of a tether.

chapters.title: What the Original Wanted
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Sef's fragmentary memories reveal the original Casper volunteered to be first backup—to guard the colony's minds at the cost of ever waking whole. Emotional beat: duty's terrible nobility.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Small Things
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The crew—just the two of them, plus one waking pod—sabotage their own salvage value, dumping the Ledger's prize manifests. Emotional beat: defiant smallness.

chapters.title: Marsh's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV (brief interlude). The syndicate captain's own backstory: she lost her family to a colony that slept through a war. Emotional beat: villainy with a wound.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Approach
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The Vesperine crosses into dead space; comms die, and it's just Casper, Ila, and the hum of forty hearts in suspension. Emotional beat: the world narrowing to two people.

chapters.title: Confession at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Ila confesses she was sent to find the beacon by the colony's descendants—she's been a courier all along. Emotional beat: betrayal that was also devotion.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Again
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Gravity flickers a second time—longer now—and the beacon transmits a countdown. Something is waking the system from outside. Emotional beat: time becoming an antagonist.

chapters.title: The Relay's Door
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. They dock at the relay: an ancient station grown, not built, its corridors lit by the same frequency as the beacon. Emotional beat: awe curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: The Fourth Copy
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. The relay's archive confirms it: Casper is backup iteration four; the original has been dead for eleven years, and the beacon's 'commissioning' was Casper's own first act. Emotional beat: identity collapsing.

chapters.title: Restore or Remain
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The relay offers a choice: merge with the original's final memories and become the colony's lawful key, or refuse and stay a copy with no legal self. Emotional beat: the cruelest multiple-choice question.

chapters.title: Ila, Asked the Impossible
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. Casper asks Ila which version of them she wants. She refuses to answer—then answers honestly: the one who chose her. Emotional beat: love stated as a criterion, not a comfort.

chapters.title: Marsh at the Door
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The Ledger arrives at the relay, having followed the countdown; Marsh offers Casper the sleepers' freedom in exchange for the merge. Emotional beat: the enemy offering the righteous path.

chapters.title: The Colony That Slept
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. The full history surfaces: the backups are the last of Calloway's Reach, a colony that voted to sleep out a purge and left one navigator to remember them. Emotional beat: scale of grief.

chapters.title: Casper's Answer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper refuses the merge—not out of fear, but because the original's duty was to remember, and Casper remembers differently, and that is enough. Emotional beat: quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Breaking the Lock
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper rewrites the beacon's final function: from lock to key, waking the pods without the relay's authorization. Emotional beat: sabotage as an act of love.

chapters.title: Forty Heartbeats
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. The backups wake—confused, grieving, alive—including a second Casper who looks at Ila like a stranger. Emotional beat: joy braided with heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Other Casper
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The woken iteration three confronts Casper; they argue over who owes the colony, who owes Ila, who is real. Emotional beat: the self made plural.

chapters.title: Marsh's Choice
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Facing forty witnesses, Marsh stands down—her salvage claim worthless against living people—and warns them the purge's architects are still listening. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming a witness.

chapters.title: The Signal Races Them
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The relay transmits the colony's existence outward; the countdown hits zero as something vast answers from dead space. Emotional beat: consequences arriving.

chapters.title: Holding the Dark
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. The awakened colonists, Caspers, and Marsh's crew together mask the signal—buying the colony time, not safety. Emotional beat: solidarity in a losing battle.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper understands at last: the beacon was never a lock or a lighthouse—it was a promise that someone would still be here to say 'you're awake, you're safe.' Emotional beat: meaning found in maintenance.

chapters.title: Let It Go Dark
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper shuts the beacon down deliberately, ending eleven years of duty, and the relay goes silent behind them. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Two Navigators, One Course
chapters.summary: Ila's POV. The two Caspers divide the work—one to lead the colonists home, one to fly the Vesperine—and the choice of who goes with Ila is made without a word. Emotional beat: bittersweet parting.

chapters.title: Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The Vesperine slips toward a system with no beacon, no archive entry, no claim on them. Casper chooses to remain the fourth—the one who stayed himself. Emotional beat: identity as a decision, renewed daily.

chapters.title: When the Colony Breaks
chapters.summary: Ila's POV, closing. On a small world, the colony wakes into morning; Ila and Casper plant the beacon's core as a garden stone. The last line: some things are kept not by locks but by people who stay. Emotional beat: earned peace, tender and unfinished.
